headline: Funding flows. Contracts signed. Delays persist.
deck: This week saw significant funding rounds and contract awards, while delays continue to plague hypersonic tests.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, with the Department of Defense increasingly pulling in private sector capabilities. This funding suggests that investors are betting heavily on the need for enhanced security in low Earth orbit.
stories.soWhat: With the DoD's appetite for co-orbital capabilities growing, True Anomaly is positioned to capitalize on a lucrative market, provided it can deliver.

stories.head: Space Force awards TrustPoint $4 million for navigation
stories.body: The Space Force has awarded TrustPoint a $4 million contract to develop a C-band navigation system as a GPS alternative. This contract underscores the military's focus on redundancy in navigation systems, especially as GPS vulnerabilities become more apparent. TrustPoint's work could be pivotal in ensuring reliable navigation in contested environments.
stories.soWhat: TrustPoint's win signals a shift toward more resilient navigation solutions, which could reshape how military operations are conducted in the future.

stories.head: Star Catcher raises $65 million for power-beaming tech
stories.body: Star Catcher has raised $65 million to validate its power-beaming technology aimed at satellites. This funding comes at a time when the potential for satellite-based power delivery is gaining traction among investors. The company's approach could redefine how power is distributed in space, moving beyond traditional methods.
stories.soWhat: If Star Catcher can prove its technology works, it may open up an entirely new market for satellite services, making conventional power delivery feel antiquated.

watchlist.title: Watch for TrustPoint's navigation demo results
watchlist.body: The results of TrustPoint's navigation demonstration could set the stage for future military contracts, especially as GPS alternatives gain traction.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's next moves post-funding
watchlist.body: With $190 million in the bank, True Anomaly's strategy for scaling operations will be closely scrutinized by both investors and competitors.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser development updates
watchlist.body: As Sierra Space moves forward with its Dream Chaser variant for the DoD, any updates could signal shifts in government contracting priorities.

watchlist.title: Anticipate more funding in power tech
watchlist.body: The interest in power-beaming technologies is likely to attract further investment, especially as Star Catcher validates its approach.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
